newsitem.title: USA: Church & Dwight sees 1997 sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Church & Dwight sees 1997 sales growth.

text.p: Church & Dwight Co Inc on Thursday said stepped-up product development during the fourth quarter should support further sales growth in 1997.
The company, which makes Arm & Hammer personal care and household products, said cost reductions and strong marketing helped improve its results in 1996.

"For the year as a whole, we continued to implement cost reduction measures while supporting our brands with increased marketing expenditures. This strategy contributed to the higher operating margin as well as to higher sales," said Robert Davies III, president and chief executive.
Shares of Church & Dwight were up 1-5/8 to 24 in early afternoon trading on the Nasdaq.
Earlier Thursday the company said fourth-quarter net income jumped to $6.1 million, or $0.31 per share, from $1.8 million, or $0.09, in 1995 fourth quarter.
Sales increased by 13.7 percent to $134.5 million from $118.3 million in the comparable period last year.
